**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Admit HTTP tool requests before enforcing the wire gate**

On Linux with an admitted HIA controller release, every HIA tool call over authenticated HTTP is rejected here. In the inspected HTTP setup, `run_http_server` in `src/main.rs` constructs `StreamableHttpService` directly around `OctofsServer`, bypassing `ReaMcpTransport`, which is the only producer of the `Admitted` extension. The new HTTP body capture supports resource reads only; it never admits tool calls. Add equivalent HTTP tool-wire admission before this check so selecting the controller does not disable all HIA tools on the supported HTTP transport.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Move the controller unit tests into a sibling test file**

This new production module defines an inline `mod tests`, contrary to the explicit test-layout requirement in root `AGENTS.md`. Move these tests into a sibling test file and register it with the prescribed `#[cfg(test)]` and `#[path = "..."]` declaration; the separate `hia_controller_native_jobs_tests.rs` module already demonstrates that layout in this file.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L32-L32](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-runtime/blob/55b4422538019a02f750a49bd03ed3b89df3aa06/AGENTS.md#L32-L32)

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add the required copyright headers to the new HIA modules**

The new `hia_request_prepare.rs` omits the required `Copyright 2026 Muvon Un Limited` line, and the new `hia_wire_candidate.rs` has no license header at all. Root `AGENTS.md` explicitly requires that header on every Rust file. Add the required Apache-2.0 source headers to both modules, retaining any additional attribution.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L33-L33](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-runtime/blob/55b4422538019a02f750a49bd03ed3b89df3aa06/AGENTS.md#L33-L33)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove unwraps from production frame decoding**

Root `AGENTS.md` explicitly prohibits `.unwrap()` and `.expect()` outside tests and OnceLock initialization. This new production decoder violates that requirement, as do the additional frame-decoding unwraps in this module and `hia_request_prepare::job_lifecycle_owner`. Replace these conversions with fallible decoding or explicitly constructed fixed-size arrays; the existing length guards do not provide an exception to the repository convention.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L34-L34](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-runtime/blob/0ce79ce0e47225073fdc5394651df942eb6b98b1/AGENTS.md#L34-L34)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve symlinked interpreter support in the native supervisor**

On a Linux operator host using the Python bootstrap with a v25/v26 controller, a symlinked `hia_worker.python_executable` now makes every new HIA job fail before spawning the worker: `O_NOFOLLOW` rejects the configured interpreter with `ELOOP`. Profile validation accepts these paths, the provider passes them through unchanged, and the documented example uses `/opt/hepta-venv/bin/python3`, which is normally a symlink in a virtual environment. The previous `subprocess.Popen` path followed it successfully. Running this extracted function against `/usr/bin/python3` reproduced errno 40. Resolve and safely pin the administrator-selected target while preserving the interpreter's original argv/virtual-environment semantics, rather than rejecting an otherwise valid profile after its durable job intent has been created.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Move synchronous frame I/O out of the async filter**

The new async `run_filter` calls `seek` on a `std::fs::File` directly on the Tokio worker. Root `AGENTS.md` explicitly requires async file I/O through `tokio::fs`, without an exception for memory-backed files. Use an asynchronous file handle or move the synchronous frame preparation and rewind into a blocking boundary before invoking the filter.
